wrapper_build: CPython 3.11.15, setuptools 84.2.1, setuptools-scm 10.3.4, wheel 0.48.0, build 1.6.1; default interpreter compiler flags, GCC 15.2.0. Both use the identical cached static archive. Rebuilding the earlier candidate (6488941) this way reproduced its measured extension .text and .rodata exactly; only the embedded build path differs.
wheel_version_note: Both development wheels use SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=1.1.1.dev0 because isolated source copies have no .git metadata.

validation.same_abi3_wheel: Built with Py_LIMITED_API=0x030B0000; abi3audit --strict: 0 violations, computed baseline 3.11. The same wheel installed on CPython 3.11.15, 3.12.14, 3.13.12, 3.14.4, 3.15.0a8 (alpha) and 3.15.0: smoke checks with stdlib oracles pass on all six; tests/test_stable_abi.py 52 passed, 10 skipped (no _testcapi), and 60 passed, 2 skipped on 3.14.4
validation.CPython_full_suite: CPython 3.14.4, PYTHONDEVMODE=1, installed wheel, including both standard-library compliance files: 14625 passed, 4 skipped (compliance alone: 138 passed, 2 skipped)
validation.PyPy_full_suite: PyPy 3.11.17 (PyPy 8.0.1), including compliance and static-type immutability checks: 14597 passed, 32 skipped
validation.free_threaded_full_suite: free-threaded CPython 3.13.11 (uv build), cp313t full-API wheel, PYTHON_GIL unset, GIL stays off after import, including compliance: 14619 passed, 10 skipped (8 need _testcapi, 1 bigmem 4 GiB, 1 needs sys.gettotalrefcount)
validation.free_threaded_import: test_import_keeps_the_gil_disabled: a fresh process with PYTHON_GIL unset and no -X gil option keeps the GIL disabled after import
validation.lint: flake8, mypy (17 files), actionlint, git diff --check, strict Sphinx and twine check pass
validation.reference_replacement: Assignment-before-DECREF ordering matches the original Py_SETREF/Py_XSETREF semantics

limits: Timings and tests are from one Linux x86_64 machine; macOS, Windows (including 3.14t) and ARM64 builds and the release audit are covered by CI jobs that were not run locally
AddressSanitizer and ThreadSanitizer CI jobs are kept but were not run locally
Limited-API builds allocate codec state with malloc/free (PyMem_RawMalloc is not in the 3.11 stable ABI), so tracemalloc does not see it there; full-API builds use PyMem_RawMalloc/PyMem_RawFree
The prototype strategy study used different binaries and a repeated Python source input; do not compare its ratios with results.json
